title: Hom-complex composition and its agreement with the derived adjunction
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a ringed site small in the chosen module universe [def-weil-size-convention], with $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their unbounded derived localization $Q$ with category $D(\mathcal O)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the Hom complex $\mathcal Hom^\bullet$ [def-pur-hom-complex], total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], K-flat complexes [def-pc-kflat-complex], and $H=R\mathcal Hom$ with its fixed K-injective augmentations $\eta_F:F\to I(F)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Fix the closed symmetric monoidal structure and its canonical K-flat tensor and uncurrying models [def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model, lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal]. Write $\operatorname{tr}$ for its right-tensor adjunction and $\epsilon_{L,M}:H(L,M)\otimes^{\mathbf L}L\to M$ for its counit. Write $O=\mathcal O[0]$ and also $O$ for its derived image. For $K,L,M\in D(\mathcal O)$ define
$$c_{K,L,M}=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\epsilon_{L,M}\circ(1\otimes\epsilon_{K,L})\circ\alpha\bigr):H(L,M)\otimes^{\mathbf L}H(K,L)\to H(K,M),$$
where $\alpha$ rebrackets $(H(L,M)\otimes^{\mathbf L}H(K,L))\otimes^{\mathbf L}K$. This family is natural contravariantly in $K$, covariantly in $M$, and dinatural in $L$: for $u:L\to L'$,
$$c_{K,L',M}\circ(1\otimes H(K,u))=c_{K,L,M}\circ(H(u,M)\otimes1)$$
as maps from $H(L',M)\otimes^{\mathbf L}H(K,L)$ to $H(K,M)$. It agrees with derived Hom-complex composition as follows. For arbitrary complexes $E,J,I$, there is a unique chain map
$$\operatorname{Tot}(\mathcal Hom^\bullet(J,I)\otimes\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,J))\to\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,I)$$
whose local homogeneous formula is $f\otimes g\mapsto f\circ g$, without an extra sign. If $J,I$ are K-injective and $t:T\to\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,J)$ is a K-flat resolution, the localization of the composite of $1\otimes t$ with this chain map represents $c_{QE,QJ,QI}$ under the canonical tensor and Hom comparisons. No boundedness or perfectness is required.
